extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles for designing and teaching school courses (particularly history, geography, nature study, and science) so subject matter becomes integrated with pupil experience, grows out of social life, and fosters scientific intelligence rather than rote learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information must be informing (integration with experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information 'whether as a means or as a widening of the content of the aim--it is informing.' The insight directly gained fuses with what is told; individual experience must be capable of taking up and holding the net results of the experience of the group to which he belongs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid presenting facts as isolated statements; aim to fuse taught material with learners' direct experience so that 'new receptiveness follows upon new curiosity.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects should enlarge ordinary experience (contextualization in time and space)
rubrics_metrics.description: Geography and history supply subject matter which gives background and outlook, intellectual perspective, to what might otherwise be narrow personal actions or mere forms of technical skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach so pupils can 'place our own doings in their time and space connections' so ordinary experiences 'gain enduring substance' rather than remain 'things of the moment.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ready-made, disconnected study (no rote piles of facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: If geography and history are taught as ready-made studies... a large number of statements about things remote and alien to everyday experience are learned; activity is divided, and two separate worlds are built up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat subject matter as something to be learned merely because it is customary; avoid 'mere amassing of information' that 'makes mind wooden' and reduces curiosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply an environment that rewards curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Curiosity is not an accidental isolated possession; it is a necessary consequence of the fact that an experience is a moving, changing thing. It is the business of educators to supply an environment so that this reaching out of an experience may be fruitfully rewarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design learning contexts that encourage pupils to seek connections and reward their 'reaching out' rather than suppressing exploratory impulses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach activities to make their wider connections perceptible
rubrics_metrics.description: The task of education... is to see to it that such activities are performed in such ways and under such conditions as render these conditions as perceptible as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When teaching practical acts (cooking, walking, hammering), make physical, biological, mechanical, and chemical consequences and connections explicit rather than leaving them implicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use history and geography to furnish context and outlook
rubrics_metrics.description: The function of historical and geographical subject matter has been stated; it is to enrich and liberate the more direct and personal contacts of life by furnishing their context, their background and outlook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and use material by its capacity to 'enrich and liberate' experience, not merely because it is traditional curriculum content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithfulness to the interdependence of man and nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The difference between penetration of this information into living experience and its mere piling up... depends upon whether these studies are faithful to the interdependence of man and nature which affords these studies their justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the mutual relation of natural environment and social life; avoid treating nature as mere 'stage scenery' for human events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center educational relevance in cultural/human aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: The educational center of gravity is in the cultural or humane aspects of the subject. From this center, any material becomes relevant in so far as it is needed to help appreciate the significance of human activities and relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reconciling subfields, use human/social significance as the organizing principle rather than external compromises among specialties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fragmentary nature study; treat nature as a whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature study has suffered in schools from scrappiness of subject matter... The real remedy is to make nature study a study of nature, not of fragments made meaningless through complete removal from the situations in which they are produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present plants, animals, and phenomena in their environmental contexts (soil, air, light, human uses) to feed imagination rather than resorting to artificial personifications or isolated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use local/home geography as a starting point for expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Local or home geography is the natural starting point in the reconstructive development of the natural environment; it is an intellectual starting point for moving out into the unknown, not an end in itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating local geography as an end; use it to introduce larger geographic and cultural connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate specialized geographic branches by human relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical or astronomical, physiographic, topographic, political, commercial, geography, all make their claims... the educational center of gravity is in the cultural or humane aspects of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specialized material only insofar as it helps understand human activities and relations; otherwise leave specialization to specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: History must be connected to present social life
rubrics_metrics.description: The segregation which kills the vitality of history is divorce from present modes and concerns of social life... Knowledge of the past is the key to understanding the present. History deals with the past, but this past is the history of the present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin historical study with present problems and trace their genesis; avoid treating the past as an object divorced from current social realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use genetic (developmental) method to understand complex products
rubrics_metrics.description: Genetic method... means that the way to get insight into any complex product is to trace the process of its making,--to follow it through the successive stages of its growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach by tracing development/process (e.g., formation of institutions, nation-building, technologies) to render complex present conditions intelligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical method: use lives of persons within social context
rubrics_metrics.description: The biographical method... makes concrete and vital historic episodes. But it is misused when employed to throw into exaggerated relief the doings of a few individuals without reference to the social situations which they represent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use biographies to illustrate social forces and contexts; avoid hero-focused accounts that detach individuals from their conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use primitive and industrial history to simplify and reveal causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recourse to the primitive may furnish the fundamental elements of the present situation in immensely simplified form... Industrial history... gives insight into the successive inventions by which theoretical science has been applied to the control of nature in the interests of security and prosperity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ study of primitive conditions and industrial/economic history to reveal basics of social organization, subsistence, and technological progress, avoiding sensationalism or exoticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include intellectual history to show development of methods and ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps the most neglected branch of history in general education is intellectual history... the great heroes who have advanced human destiny are... scientific discoverers and inventors... and the artists and poets who have celebrated his struggles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach how discoveries, inventions, and artistic expression shaped social progress and the methods of knowledge, so students grasp the role of mind in history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use history for cultivating socialized intelligence and moral understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Intelligent insight into present forms of associated life is necessary for a character whose morality is more than colorless innocence... The use of history for cultivating a socialized intelligence constitutes its moral significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor analytic, context-aware historical instruction over rote moral anecdotes; aim for lasting constructive moral insight rather than temporary moralizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science education should teach the scientific method, not only logical form
rubrics_metrics.description: Science... signifies a realization of the logical implications of any knowledge. To the non-expert, however, this perfected form is a stumbling block... From the standpoint of the learner scientific form is an ideal to be achieved, not a starting point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with learners' experience (psychological/chronological method), develop methods of observation/reflection/testing, and avoid presenting perfected scientific statements as the initial subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid early introduction of technical/formal scientific statements without context
rubrics_metrics.description: Pupils begin their study of science with texts in which the subject is organized into topics according to the order of the specialist... The pupils learn a 'science' instead of learning the scientific way of treating the familiar material of ordinary experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not lead with definitions, laws, and technical vocabulary; instead, derive them from concrete problems and the historical methods by which discoveries were made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory work must be problem-connected, not ritual
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact with things and laboratory exercises... do not of themselves suffice to meet the need... The problems dealt with may be only problems of science... Our attention may be devoted to getting skill in technical manipulation without reference to the connection of laboratory exercises with a problem belonging to subject matter. There is sometimes a ritual of laboratory instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure lab exercises address real problems linked to pupils' experience and inquiry, not merely technical manipulation or ritual procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach scientific terminology and symbols through use
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific terminology... is designed... for the things placed in a cognitive system... Their significance can be learned only by use. We cannot procure understanding of their meaning by pointing to things, but only by pointing to their work when they are employed as part of the technique of knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce scientific terms as tools used within problems and methods; focus on their role in inquiry rather than on naming or pointing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize concepts as problem-solving tools, not mere definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: One has a knowledge of mathematical conceptions only when he sees the problems in which they function and their specific utility in dealing with these problems. 'Knowing' the definitions, rules, formulae, etc., is like knowing the names of parts of a machine without knowing what they do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and teach understanding by students' ability to apply concepts within relevant problems and systems, not by memorized definitions alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use science education to broaden human purposes and imaginative life
rubrics_metrics.description: The problem of an educational use of science is then to create an intelligence pregnant with belief in the possibility of the direction of human affairs by itself... The method of science engrained through education in habit means emancipation from rule of thumb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design science instruction to modify imagination and feeling, encourage forward-looking belief in progress and rational control, and avoid treating science as mere technical means to preexisting ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach the dependencies of facts to reveal logical order
rubrics_metrics.description: Science... means that the statement of subject matter is of a nature to exhibit to one who understands it the premises from which it follows and the conclusions to which it points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help learners perceive the premises, interdependencies, and logical relations among facts so subject matter approaches the 'perfected form' of knowledge through understanding, not memorization.
